title: I/O: scans and sinks, object stores by `storage_options`, a Unity catalog client
verdict: Parquet, CSV, IPC, NDJSON, Delta, Iceberg; cloud via `storage_options`; `pl.Catalog`
description: Polars scans Parquet, CSV, IPC, NDJSON, lines, Delta, Iceberg, Lance and PyArrow datasets lazily (`scan_*`), sinks Parquet, CSV, IPC, NDJSON, Delta and Iceberg from a lazy query (`sink_*`), and writes those and Avro, Excel, JSON and databases from a frame (`write_*`).
Object stores (S3, GCS, Azure, HTTP) are reached through `storage_options` or a `credential_provider` on the scans. `pl.Catalog` is a client for Unity Catalog.
reference: I/O is outside what a plan computes; sverify's `io` modules read and write the formats.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
